title: Note 28: Complete History of SAED Windfall Tax, OIDB Cess & Royalty on ONGC (FY17–FY26)
content: Under Schedule III Note 28 (Statutory Levies), ONGC pays three major production levies to the Government: (1) Royalty (10% on offshore crude/gas, 12.5% on onshore crude, 10% on onshore gas), (2) OIDB Cess (20% ad-valorem on crude oil since union budget revision), and (3) Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED / Windfall Tax) introduced by the Government of India on 1 July 2022. When Brent surged to $96.13/bbl in FY23 during the Russia-Ukraine conflict, SAED extracted ₹10,964 Cr from ONGC, pushing total Statutory Levies to a record ₹45,284.2 Cr (29.1% of Gross Revenue) and capping net crude realisation at $75.30/bbl. In FY24, fortnightly SAED revisions reduced SAED to ₹6,433.5 Cr (total levies ₹36,797.5 Cr). In December 2024 (FY25), the Government of India formally abolished SAED on domestic crude production; FY25 SAED fell to ₹3,769.8 Cr (total levies ₹30,968 Cr). In FY26, ONGC enjoyed its first full year of zero SAED windfall tax (₹0 Cr), bringing total Statutory Levies down to ₹25,999 Cr (Royalty ₹12,965 Cr + OIDB Cess ₹13,034 Cr) and saving ₹3,770 Cr YoY.

title: Notes 36 & 37: Why FY20 PAT Crashed (₹13,464 Cr) and Why FY22 PAT Tripled to ₹40,306 Cr
content: In Q4 FY20, the COVID-19 pandemic caused global crude benchmarks to crash below $25/bbl, triggering a non-cash Exceptional Impairment charge of -₹4,899 Cr (Note 36) across mature cash-generating units and cutting FY20 Standalone PAT by 49.7% to ₹13,464 Cr. In FY21, crude oil realisation averaged an 18-year low of $42.78/bbl and gas APM prices dropped to $1.96/MMBtu, depressing Gross Revenue to ₹68,141 Cr; a partial impairment reversal of +₹1,375 Cr supported FY21 PAT at ₹11,246 Cr (PBT ₹16,403 Cr). In FY22, two historic events drove Standalone PAT up 258% to ₹40,306 Cr on PBT of ₹41,040 Cr: (1) Crude oil realisation rebounded 80% to $76.96/bbl, prompting an Exceptional Impairment Reversal of +₹7,178 Cr (Note 36); and (2) ONGC elected to migrate to the new corporate tax regime under Section 115BAA of the Income Tax Act (25.168% statutory tax rate vs 34.944% earlier), resulting in a one-time Deferred Tax liability reversal of -₹8,846 Cr (Note 37) against Current Tax of ₹9,580 Cr, reducing net Tax Expense for FY22 to just ₹734 Cr (1.79% effective tax rate).

content: Under Successful Efforts Method (Ind-AS 106 / Schedule III Note 32), geological & geophysical (G&G) survey expenditure is expensed as incurred, and exploratory wells that do not establish commercial reserves are charged off as Dry Wells Written Off. In FY23, deepwater exploratory well write-offs in KG and Andaman basins spiked Exploration Costs Written Off to ₹10,031.2 Cr (Survey ₹1,980.2 Cr + Dry Wells ₹8,051 Cr). In FY24, higher exploratory success lowered write-offs to ₹5,568.5 Cr, helping Standalone PAT reach a record ₹40,526 Cr. In FY25, accelerated frontier basin appraisal caused Exploration Costs Written Off to jump by ₹4,257.3 Cr (+76.5%) to ₹9,825.8 Cr (Survey ₹2,145.8 Cr + Dry Wells ₹7,680 Cr), while commissioning of KG-DWN-98/2 Cluster-II deepwater facilities increased DD&A (Note 33) from ₹20,495.5 Cr in FY24 to ₹22,924.2 Cr in FY25 and ₹25,197.0 Cr in FY26. In FY26, Exploration Costs Written Off moderated to ₹7,790 Cr (Survey ₹1,950 Cr + Dry Wells ₹5,840 Cr).
